title: What is known about 1RB0LE_1LC1RA_1RA1LD_0LC0LA_0RE1RF_0RC---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LE_1LC1RA_1RA1LD_0LC0LA_0RE1RF_0RC---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state machine halts from blank tape. Like 1RB---_0RC0RD_1LD1RB_0LE0LC_1RA0LF_1LD1LE in this group, its tape has two parts: a stretch 1 0 1 0 … and a solid block of 1s. At the left end the stretch is on the left (0 0 0 (10)^909 1^1859); at the right end the block is on the left (0 1^238 (10)^1718). Unlike in that machine, the block does not keep its length across a trip.
verdict: The question is open, and it is now exactly a question about one orbit of a three-number map. Lean proves (kernel, core Lean) that the machine halts if and only if DeepMind's map on C(m, k, b) = 0∞ 1m (10)k C> 1b 0∞ stops, and that this happens exactly when the orbit visits a state with m = 3b + 1.

Where the run is. Iterated from C(0, 0, 2) for 3.26·1021 steps of the map (7.03·1032 machine steps): no halt. Sizes reach about 2.6·1011. The orbit came within 1 of the halting line m = 3b + 1 several times (m − 3b = 0 or 2), last at m ≈ 1.3·1011; heuristically each new decade of the step count has a small fixed chance of a halt, so a halt may well come, far out of reach.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 3,680 cells have been visited and 3,050 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: No halt in the first 7.07·10<sup>14</sup> steps (accelerated run, Quick_Sim)
claims.text: Shawn Ligocki's Quick_Sim.py (github.com/sligocki/busy-beaver, commit cc35611) with recursive rules (-r: a macro machine with a block size it picks itself and a back symbol, rules proved symbolically from repeated tape shapes, and rules whose proofs use earlier rules) runs 3,714,000 loops from blank tape without a halt, in 121 seconds of a 2-minute screen. That is more than 7.07·1014 machine steps. It is an outside program, run here without changes; it reported no rule that repeats forever, so it does not decide the machine.

claims.title: Tape shape
claims.text: At every side switch printed near 109 steps the tape is two parts: at the left end 0 0 (10)^r 1^m or 0 1 1 (10)^r 1^m (r, m = 1052, 1564 at step 989,218,161; 213, 3249 at step 996,727,782), at the right end 0 1^m (10)^r 0 (m, r = 1437, 1103 at step 972,250,598; 238, 1717 at step 996,613,780). Consecutive sizes are erratic (m at the right: 3627, 238 after left-end m = 9, 1564).

claims.title: Growth shape: power/power
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.341). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.345).

claims.title: Growth like t<sup>1/3</sup>
claims.text: After step 5·10<sup>8</sup>: 127 side switches, 3,929,109 steps apart on average (≈ 0.291·w<sup>2</sup>, w = 3679), about 6.0 cells of width per switch; fitted width exponent 0.344 after step 10<sup>7</sup>.

claims.title: How it could halt
claims.text: The halting transition is F reading 1. F is entered only from E reading 1 (moving right). So a halt is exactly E>1 1: E on a 1 with a 1 to its right.

claims.title: Halts if and only if DeepMind's map stops
claims.text: The machine halts from blank tape if and only if the orbit of DeepMind's map DM.next on states C(m, k, b) = 0∞ 1m (10)k C> 1b 0∞ from DM.start = C(0, 0, 2) stops. Proved here on this repository's machine semantics with core Lean (it used to be a cited axiom from google-deepmind/cryptids): each of the 12 clauses of the map is one of 18 symbolic rules taking the configuration of its left side to that of its right side, or to a halt (lean/DMRules.lean, written by tools/deepmind/dmproof.py from DeepMind's configuration template), and TM.halts_iff_orbit turns them into the halts-iff statement. #print axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.

claims.title: Halts if and only if the orbit visits m = 3b + 1
claims.text: The map stops only at C(2, 0, b) with b ≥ 2, and only C(1, k, 0) is sent there. A state C(m + 3, k, b + 1) always takes the sweep clause C(m + 3, k, b + 1) → C(m, k + 2, b), so from C(3B + 1, k, B) B sweeps reach C(1, k + 2B, 0) and two more steps stop the map. Hence: the machine halts from blank tape if and only if the orbit of the map from C(0, 0, 2) visits a state C(3B + 1, k, B) (B = 0 included).

claims.title: No halt in 3.26·10<sup>21</sup> steps of the map (7.03·10<sup>32</sup> machine steps)
claims.text: c/far.c iterates the proved map from C(0, 0, 2) with the sweep jumped (C(m, k, b) → C(m − 3j, k + 2j, b − j) for j = min(⌊m/3⌋, b)), counting machine steps with the step counts of the Lean rules. In 56 minutes it made 3.26·1021 map steps, 4.04·1010 walls (b = 0) and 1.62·1011 sweep starts, reaching 7.03·1032 machine steps, with m, b up to about 2.6·1011; no sweep start had m = 3b + 1. Its first map steps agree with a plain transcription of DM.next, and its step counts were checked against a direct simulation of the machine at 235 states up to step 3·106. (An earlier run, tools/collatz/c/dm9516.c, made 1012 accelerated steps, with sizes up to 1012.)

claims.title: Near misses: a halt is plausible but far away
claims.text: At a sweep start the quantity d = m − 3b decides: d = 1 halts. In the run above d was within 2 of 1 at 16 sweep starts (d = −1, 0, 2 or 3), at sizes from 6 up to about 1.3·10<sup>11</sup>, roughly once per decade of the step count. If d were a random number of size comparable to b, the expected number of hits per decade of steps would be a small constant: the machine would halt with probability 1, but after a number of steps with a long exponent. Counting sweep starts with |d − 1| ≤ 100 gives about 20 per decade of steps (between 14 and 28 in almost every decade from 10<sup>3</sup> to 10<sup>32</sup>), so about 0.1 expected hits of d = 1 per decade, about 3 over the whole run, where none occurred (a Poisson chance of about 5%: mildly surprising, not a sign of an invariant; the residues of d mod 6 near 0 are even). This is a model, not evidence either way.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Lean reduces the question exactly to whether the orbit of DeepMind's map from C(0, 0, 2) ever visits a state with m = 3b + 1; nothing known rules that out or predicts when it happens.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The tape is a block of 1s, a stretch 1010… and a second block of 1s. Lean proves that the machine halts exactly when the left block, the stretch and the right block reach sizes m, k, b with m = 3b + 1 at the start of a sweep; the orbit has come within 1 of that line, but not onto it.

facts.text: Halts if and only if DeepMind's map visits such a state (proved here in core Lean).
Machine steps without a halt (the proved map, iterated).
Near misses: sweep starts with m − 3b within 2 of 1.

sections.heading: A stretch and a block that swap sides
html: The tape at the last side switches:
The parts swap sides on every trip, but their sizes change: no rule yet.

sections.heading: Three numbers: block, stretch, block
html: Write C(m, k, b) for the tape 0∞ 1m (10)k C> 1b 0∞. DeepMind's map sends each such tape to the next one; it is proved here, clause by clause, in core Lean. Its main move is the sweep: C(m + 3, k, b + 1) → C(m, k + 2, b) in 6k + 9 steps, which trades three 1s of the left block and one of the right block for two more 10 pairs. Sweeps repeat until one block runs out.

If the right block runs out (b = 0), the wall rule turns the stretch into a new right block: C(m, k, 0) → C(m + 1, 0, 2k + 2). If the left block runs down to m = 0, 1 or 2 first, the stretch turns into a new left block, about twice as long: for example C(0, k, b + 2) → C(2k + 2, 1, b). The only way to halt is C(2, 0, b) with b ≥ 2, which only C(1, k, 0) can reach, so a halt needs a sweep run that empties both blocks together, leaving one 1: a sweep start with m = 3b + 1.
Try it: the panel applies the 12 rules of the map to the numbers. Apply the sweep ×1000 to jump.

stepper.note: Starts at C(0, 0, 2), step 2 from blank tape. The panel does the arithmetic of the proved rules; it does not simulate the machine. A halt would show as m = 2, k = 0 with b ≥ 2, where no rule applies.

sections.heading: Why the width grows like t<sup>1/3</sup>
html: The head goes back and forth across the whole tape. After step 5·108 there are 127 side switches (extensions of the tape on the other side from the last one), on average 3,929,109 steps apart, which is about 0.291·w2 for the final width w = 3679; each adds about 6.0 cells to the width. A constant gain per w2 steps gives w3 ~ t. The fitted exponent of the width after step 107 is 0.344.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.341). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.345).
After 109 steps the tape spans 3,680 cells (1,766 left of the start, 1,213 right), with a density of 1s of 0.829.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: solid block and alternating stretch, erratic sizes
summary: Lean (kernel): halts iff DeepMind's map C(m,k,b) stops, iff its orbit visits m = 3b+1. Map iterated 3.26e21 steps (7.03e32 machine steps): no halt; near misses about once per decade.
